blocks.text: InN Indonesia - Education - speaking of books and literacy, there are troubling facts about the low-level reading interest of the nation's children today.
According to UNESCO's data, Indonesia is in the second lowest state of literature.
Only 0.001 of the Indonesian people have a high reading interest. Which means only 1 in 1000 Indonesian people have an interest in reading. Indonesia is not even better than Thailand.

Ironically, the learning program of writing and writing (callip) has been ejected at a very early age. Calistung even became a standard or even a prestigious education. A lot of early children are now getting an extra study at home about the calistings.
Unfortunately, the biases of the caterpillar have nothing to do with the interest of reading the Indonesian people. Evolving of reading interest year after year has no significant change.
The gap between the callip and the low interest of reading is actually a classic problem in this nation. The actual literacy movement is not less run by governments, organizations or individuals.
The limited access to the qualified book is the primary cause of reading interest. The minimum of access to a quality book can be handled by starting to transform our library system.
Right now, our library is old-school, with a physical or manual library model in it. Our library has to start transforming into an accessible digital library.
Indonesian citizens are the fourth largest citizen with gadgets and social use of media in the world. There are estimated 100 million people playing gadgets every day.
The Indonesian people also have the longest access to gadgets seven to eight hours a day. Looking at the data, it's supposed to be digital literature being an important part of Indonesian education.
Schools also have to start setting up a digital catering program that starts with early-age education.
Indonesia needs a bold move even said to be reckless in the pursuit of literacy.
The government can build a digital library system connected to international top journals or source of international digital books, but it's cheap or free access.
We need to imitate the crazy steps Japan makes after losing the American war, which is buying and accessing books and then making easy access to society.
Without a brave and crazy move like this don't expect Indonesia to catch up with literature.
